runbook: R-18 / R-19 independent oracle (fresh investigator, blind to the change)

evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
read: data/champions.json (base AD / base armor growth for all 173 champions)
data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json, data/worklists/*, data/onhit-matrix.json (searched, no scenario definition present)
evidence_tree.limitation: The golden scenario definition (participants, levels, builds, target resistances) lives in scripts/golden_snapshot.py, which is outside the permitted evidence tree and is not mirrored anywhere under data/. The computation below is therefore a feasibility/envelope proof on the two named items rather than a point reproduction of the scenario inputs.

sources_quoted.text: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
Armor and magic resistance reduce incoming physical/magic damage by a percentage (actual = raw x 100/(100 + resistance)); negative resistances amplify damage.
percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.

m(R) = 100 / (100 + R); 'Flat armor reduction can reduce armor values below 0, while percentage armor reduction cannot' (League Wiki, Armor penetration) -- so Carve's percentage shred cannot drive armor below 0, hence m <= 1 for any champion target.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md audit table (Stat growth) + CLAUDE.md domain rule
sources_quoted.text: base + growth x (L-1) x (0.7025 + 0.0175 x (L-1)); at L18 the growth factor is exactly 1.0, so stat18 = base + 17 x growth.

step_2_legitimate_multiplier_envelope_fo.carve_max: sup over armor A of (100+A)/(100+0.7A) = 1/0.7 = 1.42857 (5 stacks, 30% armor reduction, floor at 0 per the wiki rule)
step_2_legitimate_multiplier_envelope_fo.expose_weakness_max: x1.08 (melee branch of {{rd|8%|5%}}); multiplicative per damage.modifier
step_2_legitimate_multiplier_envelope_fo.conclusion: 2.4139 > 1.5429. No admissible modeling of Carve + Expose Weakness can account for the gap; the two values differ in the damage source term or in whether mitigation was applied at all, not in the item modifiers.

step_3_feasibility_bound_on_the_old_valu.premise: The only damage packet either named item authors is Bloodsong's Spellblade proc: raw = 100% BASE AD, physical, on-hit.

min_champion_base_armor_at_L18.champion: Thresh (33 base, 0 growth - soul-scaled); next lowest is Anivia 88.7

step_3_feasibility_bound_on_the_old_valu.conclusion: 121.85 < 128.9. Even the single highest-base-AD champion in the cache, hitting the single lowest-armor champion in the cache with zero armor items and a full 5-stack Carve, cannot produce 128.9 from a 100%-base-AD proc. (Adding Expose Weakness gives 131.6, but the wiki text states the debuff 'starts after using the empowered attack', so the applying proc is not self-amplified.) 128.9 is therefore outside the feasible range; 53.4 is comfortably inside it.

step_4_reconstructions_that_reproduce_bo.reading: Spellblade read TOTAL AD instead of BASE AD
step_4_reconstructions_that_reproduce_bo.math: base AD 106.1 (L18), target armor 141.0 -> Carve 30% -> 98.7 -> m = 100/198.7 = 0.50327 -> 106.1 x 0.50327 = 53.40 (new). Bonus AD 150.0 (Black Cleaver 40 + two ~55 AD legendaries) -> total AD 256.1 -> 256.1 x 0.50327 = 128.9 (old). Ratio 256.1/106.1 = 2.4139, matching exactly.
step_4_reconstructions_that_reproduce_bo.wiki_ruling: The cached wiki text says 100% '''base''' AD. Total-AD basis is wrong; the smaller value is correct.

step_4_reconstructions_that_reproduce_bo.math: 128.9 x 100/(100+R) = 53.4 solves at R = 141.4 -- i.e. the old value is the raw pre-mitigation number and the new value is the same packet mitigated by 141.4 effective armor (e.g. 202 armor shredded 30% by Carve).
step_4_reconstructions_that_reproduce_bo.wiki_ruling: Physical damage is mandatorily mitigated by armor (damage.resistance-mitigation; math-foundations Sec. 2.1). The mitigated value is correct.

independent_computation.verdict_logic: Every reading that reproduces the 2.4139 gap from the cached wiki text has the OLD value overstating a capped effect (total-AD basis for a base-AD proc, or unmitigated raw), and the new value inside the feasible envelope. The old value is additionally excluded outright by the step-3 upper bound of 121.85 for a 100%-base-AD Spellblade proc against any champion. No reading found in which 53.4 under-states a wiki-sourced quantity.

residual_uncertainty: The scenario's participants, levels, builds and target resistances could not be read (they live in scripts/, outside the evidence tree), so the event-46 packet is identified by item semantics rather than by direct reproduction. If events[46]/pair_damage is not a Bloodsong Spellblade packet but an aggregate over a paired participant, the step-3 bound does not bind and only the step-2 envelope argument (old/new = 2.41 is unreachable from Carve+Expose Weakness) survives - which still favours the new value. Confidence: high on direction, medium on exact packet identity.
